before.title: Cylinder Deactivation Valvetrain Tapping/Rattle (Switchable HLA Air Entrapment) - SA-026/23
before.description: CX-30s with the 2.5L naturally aspirated SkyActiv-G equipped with cylinder deactivation can develop a tapping/rattling noise from the valve train area. Mazda traces it to the switchable hydraulic lash adjusters (HLAs) used by cylinder deactivation, which malfunction when air bubbles accumulate in the oil passage. Note: cylinder deactivation was offered on 2020 and again 2023-2025 CX-30s (not 2021-2022).
before.solution: Per Mazda Service Alert SA-026/23, the procedure is to purge trapped air (running the engine at ~2,500-3,000 rpm) and, where the noise persists, replace the switchable HLAs with a revised version (a revised service cylinder head assembly has also been established) to reduce air entrapment.
symptoms: Tapping or rattling from the valve train / top of engine
Noise more noticeable at idle or low rpm
Vibration or shudder when cylinder deactivation engages

proposal.title: Cylinder Deactivation Valvetrain Tapping/Rattle (Switchable HLA Air Entrapment) - SA-026/23

proposal.solution: For a vehicle inside SA-026/23, first check engine-oil level, warm the engine and follow Mazda's purge and road-test sequence. If the noise remains, Mazda directs the technician to contact its hotline; this alert does not prescribe automatic HLA or cylinder-head replacement. Other model years or persistent noise require oil-pressure and valvetrain diagnosis. Do not buy HLAs or a cylinder head from this page; verify VIN, engine equipment, oil condition and the applicable service document first.
symptoms: tapping or rattling from the upper engine after storage or repeated short cold starts
noise may change after the engine is warmed and held near 2,500-3,000 rpm
persistent noise requires separate oil-pressure and valvetrain diagnosis

symptoms: Fuel smell or visible fuel leak from rear of vehicle after a full tank fill-up
Engine stalls while driving

before.title: Excessive Oil Consumption (2.5 Turbo) - Low Oil Warning Between Changes
before.description: Owners of 2021-2022 CX-30 2.5 Turbo models report the low engine oil level warning illuminating only a few thousand miles after service with no visible external leaks, indicating oil burning in the combustion chamber (some owners see warnings well under 10,000 miles, recurring every ~3,000-4,000 miles). before.solution: Mazda issued a TSB (#01-012-21-3832a) for the low oil level warning / check engine light as a temporary measure (top off and reset); Mazda later recommended replacing the exhaust valve stem seals, which resolved the consumption. A valve stem seal class-action settlement (2021-2022 2.5T CX-30, Mazda3, CX-5, CX-9, Mazda6) provides seal replacement, an extended 84-month/84,000-mile powertrain warranty, and reimbursement of out-of-pocket oil costs. Owners should monitor and document oil level between changes.
symptoms: Low engine oil level warning between scheduled oil changes
No visible oil leaks or drips under the car
Possible check engine light
Repeated need to top off oil

This issue is documented through owner complaints and forums rather than an official campaign.

proposal.description: Mazda Service Alert SA-007/24 documents situations in which Smart Brake Support can activate because the forward camera or radar interprets curves, overhead structures, roadside objects, grade changes, trees, bicycles or turning vehicles as a collision risk. event may occur near curves, signs, roadside objects, grade changes, trees, bicycles or turning vehicles

before.title: A/C Condenser Leak
before.description: The A/C condenser in the CX-30 is prone to developing pinhole leaks from road debris impact and corrosion. The condenser sits exposed behind the front grille with minimal protection. Refrigerant loss causes gradual A/C performance degradation until the system stops cooling entirely.
before.solution: Replace A/C condenser and recharge system with R-134a refrigerant. Install a condenser stone guard or grille screen to protect from future debris impact. Check for secondary leaks at hose connections during replacement.
symptoms: A/C blows warm air gradually worsening over weeks
A/C works intermittently - cool in morning, warm in afternoon
Visible oily residue on A/C condenser (refrigerant leak)
A/C compressor cycles on and off rapidly (low charge)

proposal.title: A/C Condenser Leak
proposal.description: Mazda Service Alert SA-053/21 covers certain 2020-2021 CX-30 vehicles below its VIN and October 22, 2020 production cutoffs when the A/C blows warm because refrigerant charge is low. It directs leak diagnosis and specifically identifies an evaporator leak as a possible cause. The reviewed primary inventory does not establish the frozen title's recurring condenser defect, road-debris mechanism, corrosion mechanism or a 2020-2025-wide pattern.
proposal.solution: Have a qualified A/C technician verify refrigerant charge and locate the leak before replacing anything. For a vehicle within SA-053/21, Mazda directs inspection of the evaporator if charge is low and no other leak is found; the expansion valve is replaced only if it leaks. Verify the under-hood refrigerant label because the bulletin covers both HFC-134a and HFO-1234yf vehicles. Do not buy a condenser, evaporator, expansion valve, refrigerant or stone guard from this page; confirm VIN, refrigerant type and exact leak location first.
symptoms: A/C blows warm or cooling performance declines
system inspection shows low refrigerant charge
leak testing is required to distinguish evaporator, condenser, valve or connection faults

before.description: The Mazda Connect infotainment system in CX-30 frequently freezes, reboots, or loses Apple CarPlay/Android Auto connection. before.title: Windshield Stress Cracking
before.description: CX-30 windshields are prone to developing stress cracks without external impact. The acoustic laminated glass used for noise reduction appears more susceptible to temperature changes and frame flex. Cracks often originate from the edges or near the base of the windshield. Multiple NHTSA complaints have been filed.
before.solution: Windshield replacement with OEM or equivalent acoustic glass. Safelite and other glass shops can install. If no impact point is visible, submit claim to Mazda for goodwill coverage as a manufacturing defect. ADAS camera recalibration required after replacement.
symptoms: Crack appears on windshield without visible impact point
Crack typically starts at windshield edge and spreads
More common in areas with large temperature swings
May start as a small chip that rapidly propagates

communityRecommendations.content: OEM Mazda acoustic windshield for CX-30 (ensure ADAS camera compatible)
